newsitem.title: USA: CME nearby lumber ends limit-down, Nov overbought.
newsitem.headline: CME nearby lumber ends limit-down, Nov overbought.

text.p: CME November, January and March lumber futures ended down the daily $10.00-per-thousand-board- feet daily trading limit, pressured by ideas that the market was oversold and by commodity fund selling, CME floor traders said.
"The sense today (Wednesday), is that November is really overbought," one pit trader said. "This doesn't have much to do with fundamentals."
The pool of sell-orders in November was estimated at 90 lots, and the pool in January was said to be 120 lots, pit sources said.
FIMAT Futures Inc and LIT America were noted buyers in November in early trade, while Prudential Securities and E.D. and F. Man were prominent sellers early, traders said.
The U.S. Commerce Department released new home sales data Wednesday, but the report was seen as neutral to slightly supportive, lumber analysts and traders said.

At 816,000 homes, new home sales in September were down 0.5 percent from August sales, but that drop was not considered significant when compared with a 10-year high in new homes sales during the previous month, lumber analysts said.
Traders were also anxiously awaiting trade data from the Canadian government, which is said to be set for release Thursday. The quota information is generally expected to be supportive for futures.
November lumber settled down $10.00 tbf at $412.20, and January closed down $10.00 at $374.40. Other contracts closed down $10.00 to down $7.40 tbf.
